title: Quarterly scenario framework for hosted API + model catalog (decision criteria & contingency mapping)
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Purpose: define a compact, decision-oriented scenario framework for the upcoming quarter that ties hosted API capacity, model catalog selection, and rollout gates to explicit metrics and contingency actions. This doc enables PM, Eng, and SRE to quickly choose a pre-approved path (Optimistic / Base / Conservative) when external signals (usage growth, cost, latency regressions, infra failures) change the operating envelope.

Scope: hosted API capacity planning, model variants and quantization choices exposed in the catalog, canary windows and rollback triggers, and an operations playbook for cross-tier fallbacks. Not in scope: long-term model research prioritization or per-customer enterprise contracts (those will be handled by separate enterprise queues).

Key outcomes we want by end of cycle: 1) A signed decision matrix that maps metrics -> scenario, 2) a set of pre-curated fallback model bundles per scenario, 3) runbook steps for throttling/burst controls and canary rollback, 4) measurement dashboards (p95 latency, token cost per 1k, error rate, model quality delta) instrumented for each route in Console.
updates: 2026-01-10: Initial draft created and shared with Eng and SRE for input. Core asks enumerated: (a) decision gates, (b) fallback bundles, (c) dashboard signals.

2026-01-12: Engineering sync — runtime team (Khan, Priya) confirmed ability to expose per-route p95 and in-flight batching histograms. Noted caveat: KV cache hit metrics require small server patch (ENG-1842) before dashboards are fully reliable.
2026-01-15: SRE provided a template for capacity tranches and emergency scale-up steps. Suggested conservative tranche should assume -30% KV cache effectiveness to stress test fallback models.
2026-01-18: Design reviewed proposed dashboard wireframes. Feedback: make model quality delta visually prominent and add annotation layer for canary windows and outages.
2026-01-21: PM review — updated decision matrix with explicit numeric thresholds for scenario triggers (see links). Added dependency on release automation work for canary rollouts (ENG-5019).
2026-01-25: Stakeholder readout scheduled next week. Action items: finalize fallback bundle definitions, add runbook steps for token-throttling, and tag release branch for hostedapi-2026.04.
2026-02-02: (Follow-up) Added a contingency for model-quality regressions: automatic reroute to verified smaller model + human alert to MLE triage channel.
comments: Priya (Eng): We can support temporary model pinning per customer but it needs interface work in the Console. Recommend adding a 2-week engineering spike to scope UI changes.
Khan (Runtime): Kernel selection profiles need to be versioned when we expose quantized variants. Without that we risk silent perf regressions during rotation.
Asha (Design): Dashboard needs an 'incident context' panel that surfaces recent canary decisions and the last time a fallback bundle was used.
Tom (SRE): For conservative scenario, include concrete steps to enable rate-limiting at the CDN edge and enable cost-shedding headers for non-critical routes.
Evan (Sales): Include a note for enterprise customers: we should surface recommended private deployment or Dedicated capacity if they opt out of automatic fallbacks.
Leah (PM): Added acceptance criteria — decision matrix signed off by Eng/SRE/Design and a staging dashboard showing synthetic workloads for each scenario.
